title: EV charging for new buildings: developers and designers | VOOL
description: What EU rules require for charging in new and renovated buildings, how to size the connection, and specification text for tenders.

sections.title: Design charging into the building once, and size the connection smaller
sections.lead: New buildings must be prepared for charging. With load management at several fuse levels, the charging load fits a connection sized for the building.
sections.alt: Underground car park with VOOL chargers

sections.title: What the EU rules require
paragraphs: The recast Energy Performance of Buildings Directive sets minimum requirements for new buildings and major renovations. Member states apply them through national law and may go further, so check the local rules.
points: New residential buildings with more than three parking spaces: pre-cabling for at least half of the spaces, ducting for the rest, and at least one charging point.
New non-residential buildings with more than five parking spaces: at least one charging point for every five spaces, pre-cabling for at least half and ducting for the rest.
Charging points must be capable of smart charging.
Chargers installed from 1 January 2027 must also support ISO 15118-20. See AFIR and ISO 15118.

items.title: Smaller connection
items.text: The LMC measures the building’s real load and gives the rest to the cars. One site runs 45 chargers on a 125 A connection.

items.title: Several fuse levels
items.text: Limits are respected at the main fuse, at sub-distribution boards and on each charger line.

items.title: Phase switching
items.text: Chargers move single-phase cars to the least loaded phase, so the three phases stay balanced.

items.title: Build in stages
items.text: Install cabling and the LMC with the building. Owners add chargers later, each one in minutes.

items.title: Ready for billing
items.text: Each owner or tenant pays for their own charging. The association or operator issues no invoices.

items.title: Open protocols
items.text: OCPP, Modbus TCP and OCPI, so the building is not locked to one operator.

sections.title: Specification text for tenders
paragraphs: Copy and adapt this text. It describes functions, so it does not exclude other makers who can deliver the same.
points: AC charging points up to 22 kW (3 × 32 A) with Type 2 connector, IP54 or better and IK10.
Dynamic load management that measures the building’s total consumption in real time and limits charging so that the main fuse and every sub-distribution fuse stay within their rating.
Load management at a minimum of two levels of the electrical installation, for at least 100 charging points per controller.
Automatic phase switching or phase balancing between charging points.
Load management continues to work when the internet connection is down.
Communication: OCPP 1.6 or later. Chargers installed from 1 January 2027: ISO 15118-2 and ISO 15118-20.
Software for user management, RFID or app authorisation, pricing per user group and billing per user, with consumption reports for the building owner.
Interface to the building management system over Modbus TCP.
Manufacturer’s warranty of at least five years on charging points.
